versions.model: A version is a workspace folder holding a full KB. Workspaces form a tree through based-on.
versions.branch: intent-format branch <root> <from> <to>: copy the workspace, set version, lifecycle: in-progress, based-on: <from>.
versions.fingerprint: Per card, by core, against the base workspace's current content. Parts: Passport (front matter except standard, plus the title name) and each authored section by heading (incl. unknown and x- sections; sub-documents count in their host section). Before comparing: references reduced to #CORE, anchor lines, status line and ⚙ lines removed, trailing spaces trimmed, blank-line runs collapsed.

results.new: core absent from the base workspace

operations.duplicate: Manual: copy the file, take a new core from intent-format mint, rename the file; no provenance stamp.
operations.merge: Manual: rebind every reference (incl. feature:/parent:) to the survivor, delete the other file, add its core to ⚙ Retired with Merged into = survivor. The survivor keeps its own origin.
operations.promotePlaceholder: Manual edit: replace [~ Name] with a reference to the card that now exists. check reports exact matches (info); regen never promotes.

import: Re-mint every core (cards and sub-documents) into the project counters.
Rewrite references inside the imported set to the new cores.
References to targets outside the set become placeholders with a note: [~ <Name>] — was #<core> in <kb>.
Rewrite feature:/parent: when the target is in the set; otherwise drop the key and report an info diagnostic.
Never trust shipped ⚙ content: strip it and regenerate.
exchange.reimport: A card whose origin: <kb>/<core> already exists in the project is skipped with a warning. No content hash.

extensions.registration: None. Any X*/Z* prefix, type x-<slug>, x-* key, ## x-<name> section or x-<slug> relation is accepted and preserved untouched.
extensions.relationLines: Extension relations always carry their explicit prefix: - x-<slug>: <atom>…

perspectives: Grouping by feature, state, platform or status (and variant-level involvement) is a computed view in tools; nothing is stored for it.

blindSpot.meaning: Unknown — a declared blind spot. Counted in health when the section is required (or is a sub-document body).

verifiedNone.meaning: Authored and verified: there is nothing here. Not counted.

incompleteList.meaning: The final item of a list in a section with a default relation, written - — or N. —: more items exist but are unknown. A blind spot (kind lists); not a bad line shape.

forgiveness.meaning: Read as — (info); regen rewrites them to —.

bodyStates.alone: — and none are body states only when they are the whole body (a single line).
bodyStates.absent: An optional section that is absent = nothing to say (not a blind spot). A required section that is absent = missing (warning).

values.—: nobody has asked yet — missing; counted as a blind spot of kind why (the health line calls it why debt)
values.none: no why needed here (a divider, a plain button); may carry a note: none — layout only. Not counted.
values.same as #XX000000: another card's why covers this one — any card, named by its core id. check follows the link; a target with no why makes this card count as missing [I030]; an id that names no card, or the card itself, is a warning [W051].

confidence.assumed: [assumed] — a guess no input supports; an open question and a blind spot

# Example app · #PR000001
> ⚙ #PR000001V1.0 · V1.0 in-progress

## Description
A small app in which a Member keeps a list of items: create, browse and change them.


## Why
Members lose track of things kept in notes and chats; one list that is always at hand fixes that.
## User stories
- As a Member, I want to create an item, so that I can keep track of it.
- As a Member, I want to browse my items, so that I find one quickly.
- As a Member, I want to edit an item, so that its details stay current.
- As a Member, I want to change my settings, so that the app fits how I work.
- As an Admin, I want to review all items, so that the list stays clean.

## Keep in mind

- [ ] Every screen works with the keyboard alone.

grammar.note: Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions used with the u flag; named groups are the parse result.

shapes.statusLine: > ⚙ <rendered-id> · V<version> <lifecycle>[ · based on V<base>][ · new | unchanged | changed: <Part>, <Part>]
shapes.bodies: — alone = blind spot · none alone = verified none

lineParsing: Match listLine: marker "- " or "<n>. ", leading spaces = indentation.
A ⚙ directly before a relation word marks a machine-owned line (⚙ Prev / ⚙ Next).

relationPrefix with a vocabulary word (or x-<slug>) → explicit relation; else, in a section with a default relation, a body that starts with an atom (step lists: optionally after a glyph) → prefix-less line; else prose.
Entry / Outcome: the rest is one text value; atoms inside are mentions. Stop.
Split off the note at the first " — " outside [], () and "…".
Edge and Branch: split at the first " → " outside [], () and "…" (left: atom, or the Branch label).
Split the rest at " · " outside [], () and "…": first part = the atom, the others = qualifiers.
Parse the atom: bound | hand | placeholder | — ; anything else is a bad line shape.
grammar.mentions: In prose, bound and hand references are untyped mentions: resolved and refreshed, never a relation. Placeholders in prose count as unresolved.

ask.where: inside any authored body line of any card, in the sentence it concerns; never in front matter, a generated section or a status line
ask.means: a question for the owner that no card value can hold yet: an unknown fact, a doubt about a sentence. Not a blind spot (— says 'unknown'), not a guess ([assumed] says 'probably')
ask.counted: health asks {open, later, due}; intent-format open lists each with its card, due ones first; never a blind spot
ask.closed: the answer rewrites the sentence and the marker goes. "Later" (the owner's word) adds · later <date> and keeps it counted; after `again` days (2) it is due and asked again. Only the owner closes a question as not relevant; the agent never drops one. "Unknown" is not an answer: the question stays.
